Personal Property Online Assessment
In order to log in through the link below use your account number and pin mailed out in early January and once logged in; buttons at the bottom of each page will guide you through each step of the process.
Begin your Online Personal Property Assessments
We wish to thank all of the Clay County taxpayers for their feedback and their patience. As always, if you do not prefer to file your assessment online please call our office at 816-407-3500 option 3; and we will notate this on your account so you can receive the paper Assessment form.
Personal Property Waivers
If you are a new Missouri resident or haven't owned a vehicle in more than a year you may be entitled to a waiver. You will need to bring to the office your title, application for title, or out-of-state registration. We will review your paperwork and issue the waiver at that time with minimal waiting.
If you have been a Clay County resident and owned a vehicle but didn't receive a tax bill it's possible you weren't assessed and need to be. You can call our office at 816-407-3520 to check if you've been assessed before driving to one of our locations. If you have not, you will need to come into one of our locations to fill out the assessment paperwork and have a tax bill generated.
If you need to tag a vehicle that isn't on your tax receipt and you did own it on January 1st of the previous year, you will need to come into one of our locations to have it added to your tax bill. If you purchased the vehicle after January 1st of the previous year, it will not need to be on your tax receipt. You are only taxed on the property you owned on January 1st of each year.
Real Estate Reassessment
All County Assessors in Missouri are required to value real estate property in the county as of January 1st of each odd-numbered year.
If the assessed value of your property increases, a Change-of-Value Notice will be mailed to you.
The window to schedule an informal meeting with the Assessor's office is now closed. A value appeal can be made through the Board of Equalization . The appeal must be submitted by July 13, 2026.
Visit our Real Estate Page for more information.
If you have any questions, please contact our office. We will be glad to assist you.
The Assessor's Office is tasked to ensure that the tax burden is distributed equitably among all property owners. To accomplish this all property is valued with uniform and consistent processes and procedures following Missouri Revised Statutes.
The Personal Property section provides you with a connection to many of the personal and business property assessment lists and forms used by the Assessor's Office, along with a comprehensive list of FAQs for business and personal property.
The Real Estate section provides a connection to resources including a Parcel Search that provides valuation and appraisal information, and Change of Valuation Notices.
The GIS/Mapping division creates, manages, and publishes land parcel data using current geographical information system (GIS) technology. Custom maps are available for purchase.
